content.thinking: I'm going to drop the line about nothing catching the error, since that's not right. Step 4 about the failure taking down the page request seems fine as it is. I'm wondering whether to add a contributing factor about the unhandled error, but I'll keep it simple: the root cause is that the code raises a ZeroDivisionError, and the account page request fails because of it.

action_items.item: Fix the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 so that a zero divisor no longer raises an error.
Keep monthly-spend-feature off until the fix to src/io_shop/spend_summary.py is merged and deployed.
Roll out feature flags in production to a small share of traffic first, and turn the flag off automatically if the error rate rises after the change.
Require that code behind a feature flag is tested with the flag on, including edge-case account data such as zero values, before the flag can be switched on in production.
Make the account page still render, without the spend summary, when the spend-summary section raises an error.

causal_chain.step: The requests failed with a ZeroDivisionError raised at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, starting in the minute the incident began. Before that minute, the only account-page failures logged were shoppers closing the connection.

ruled_out.what: A deploy or a revision change: no deploy came back from the window that was read, the flag change was the only production change read back, and account pages rendered normally with the running revision in place before the onset.
A different flag change: the flag provider's history showed only this one flag change by anyone other than Argus in the hour that was read.
Shoppers closing their connections: these errors were logged while the service ran normally before the onset, and stopped being logged before it.

causal_chain.step: That code ran because admin switched the monthly-spend-feature flag on at {P1.1}. The flag read off on every evaluation before that minute, was split between off and on during that minute, and read on for every evaluation after it.
The code path behind the flag divides by a value that is zero for some account page requests, and those requests fail with the resulting error.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly-spending feature sent account pages through new code that divided by zero for some shoppers, so their account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag was switched from off for all traffic to on for all traffic within a single minute. No staged rollout, and no automatic check of the error rate tied to the flag change, was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: If the flag had been turned on for a small share of shoppers first, with an automatic error-rate check, only that share would have hit the failure, and the flag could have been turned back off before most account pages were affected.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test or pre-enablement check was seen that ran the spend-summary path with the flag on against account data that gives a zero divisor.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Such a test would have raised the ZeroDivisionError before the flag was switched on in production, and the flag would have stayed off until the code was fixed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: No handling was seen that keeps an error in the spend-summary section from failing the whole account page.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Account pages could still have loaded without the spend summary, so shoppers would not have seen failed pages.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident in the same minute as the flag change.
The Investigator Agent formed a single candidate cause that named the flag change and the ZeroDivisionError in the logs.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature back off. The action can be undone.
Some Person kept the flag off and paged the checkout team.

input.root_cause: The spend-summary code that monthly-spend-feature turns on raises a ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 for some account page requests, and those requests fail with that error. The evidence does not show why the divisor is zero for those requests.
input.still_at_risk: If anyone switches monthly-spend-feature back on before the spend-summary code is fixed, account pages could fail the same way again.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
